title: Uniform cohomological bounds in the finite-type range
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $X,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type. Use small sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ put $d_T=\dim T$ if $T\ne\varnothing$ and $d_T=0$ if $T=\varnothing$, and put $e_T=2d_T+1$; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, where torsion means every local section is locally killed by a positive integer [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], without a uniform annihilator. Write $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ for comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Restrictions along a scheme map mean the corresponding inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Cohomology means right-derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

1. If $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ is a pro-étale affine presentation over $X$ [sk-def-pe-morphisms], with $U$ an object of $X_{\Proet}$ and $U_i$ affine étale over $X$, then $H^q(U_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*G)|_U)=0$ for $q>e_X$.
2. If $V=\varprojlim_iV_i$ is such a presentation over $Y$, with $V$ an object of $Y_{\Proet}$ and $V_i$ affine étale over $Y$, then, writing $T=X\times_YV$ for the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product],
$$H^q(T_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*G)|_T)=0\qquad(q>e_X).$$
3. The higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] satisfies $R^qg_{\Et,*}G=0$ for $q>e_X$.

Each presentation has a small nonempty cofiltered index category and affine transition maps. The same assertions apply with $Y$ as source, a torsion sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$, and bound $e_Y$ (and any finite-type map from $Y$ to a finite-type $k$-scheme).

proof.text: First prove the all-torsion field bound that the opening paragraph needs, rather than infer it from a bound for a single prime. Choose a separable closure and an algebraic closure of $k$ containing it. The additive stalk equivalence [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] and the natural invariant-section formula [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] identify derived sections with derived invariants: an additive equivalence and its inverse preserve kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, and preserve injectives by the Hom lifting criterion. Applying the equivalence to an injective resolution therefore gives an injective resolution and the section complexes are naturally isomorphic. By [det-base-field-cd-cochains], part 1, $H^s(k_{\Et},F)=H^s(G_k,F_{\bar k})$. A torsion sheaf has torsion stalk: a germ is represented by a section and a covering on which that section is killed supplies an integer killing the germ.

If $k$ is finite, [det-base-field-cd-galois-group] identifies $G_k$ with $\widehat{\mathbf Z}$. Pullback of cochains along this topological group isomorphism commutes with the written cochain differential and has inverse pullback along its inverse. For a torsion discrete module $M$, every element $x$ has finite orbit: its open stabilizer contains a coordinate kernel $\ker(\widehat{\mathbf Z}\to C_m)$, since a basic open neighbourhood restricts finitely many coordinates and their least common multiple dominates them. If $ex=0$, the subgroup generated by its orbit of size $t$ is an image of $(\mathbf Z/e)^t$, hence finite and stable. Finite sums of such subgroups are finite. They form a small nonempty directed family (a subset of the power set of $M$, containing zero), whose union is $M$. Part 2 of [det-base-field-cd-cochains] reduces vanishing to finite stable modules.

source.place: Reduction to finite modules; Consequences, finite-field Galois group

proof.text: For a finite stable module $A$, choose $e\ge1$ with $eA=0$. The intersection of the finitely many open stabilizers is an open action kernel, containing a coordinate kernel $K_m$; hence the action factors through $C_m$. Coordinate kernels $K_n$, $m\mid n$, are cofinal among open normal subgroups acting trivially on $A$: given such an $N$, a basic neighbourhood gives $K_d\subseteq N$, and $K_{\operatorname{lcm}(m,d)}\subseteq N$. Projections onto $C_n$ are surjective, since compatible residues of integers give every residue. Thus part 3 of [det-base-field-cd-cochains] gives $H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},A)=\varinjlim_{m\mid n}H^s(C_n,A)$. For $s\ge2$, inflation from $n$ to $en$ is zero by the final clause of [det-base-field-cd-inflation], with multiplier $r=e$. Every colimit class therefore becomes zero. Together with steps 1–2 this proves $H^s(k,F)=0$ for every torsion sheaf and $s>1$. If $k$ is algebraically closed it is separably closed, and [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives the stronger vanishing for $s>0$. In both cases $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)\le1$, in exactly the all-torsion sense of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], X and Y have finite Krull dimension. The definition [def-kun-dimension] uses the same chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets as [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], so their dimensions agree. A nonempty scheme has a length-zero chain by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] applied to a point closure; hence each nonempty source dimension is a nonnegative integer and e_X and e_Y are finite nonnegative integers. Record the finite-type and quasi-separated hypotheses before applying a limit theorem. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. Every affine étale $W\to X$ or $W\to Y$ is of finite type over $k$: étale is locally finitely presented [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally finitely generated; composing finite generating sets gives local finite type over $k$, and $W$ is quasi-compact because it is affine [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $T_i=X\times_YV_i$, first show quasi-compactness. Cover $Y$ by finitely many affine opens $Y_b$. By finite type of $g$, each $g^{-1}(Y_b)$ has a finite affine cover by schemes whose coordinate rings are finitely generated over the ring of $Y_b$. Since $V_i$ is a finite-type affine $k$-scheme, it is Noetherian by the cited theorem; its open inverse image of each $Y_b$ has a finite affine cover. The products of these two finite covers give a finite affine cover of $T_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. These are open subsets covering $T_i$: for opens $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq V_i$ mapping to a common open of $Y$, the open $p_X^{-1}(A)\cap p_V^{-1}(B)$, with its restricted structure sheaf, has the fibre-product universal property for $A,B$ over that open. Every point lies in such a pair, so their finite collection covers. In particular $T_i$ is quasi-compact. Its map to $X$ is étale by base change (used explicitly in step 5), so it is locally of finite type over $k$ via $X$; together these give finite type. Thus all stage schemes are Noetherian by the same cited theorem and are qcqs: intersections of affine opens are opens of a Noetherian topological space, hence quasi-compact. The topological assertion follows from [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]: among complements of finite unions from an open cover choose a minimal one; adding each other open cannot shrink it, so that finite union covers the given open. Quasi-separatedness also follows directly from [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. No separatedness of $X,Y,g$ and no compatibility of $g$ with the given $k$-structures is used.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); affine definitions of finite type and base change

proof.text: For any étale morphism $a:W\to X$, [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] applied on affine neighbourhoods gives $\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,a(w)}$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], every chain of generalizations beginning at $w$ has length at most $\dim X$. Conversely, any finite chain of irreducible closed subsets of $W$ gives a chain of their generic points, which exist uniquely by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], beginning at the generic point of the smallest member. The same cited chain formula bounds its length by $\dim X$. The definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] then gives $\dim W\le\dim X$. This works for nonseparated schemes and does not require the image of $a$ to be closed. For $W=T_i$ use étale stability under base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits].

Suppose $X\ne\varnothing$. For every nonempty finite-type $W$ étale over $X$, steps 3 and 5 allow [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] with $c=1$, yielding $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(W)\le2\dim W+1\le e_X$. For empty $W$, all sheaves and their section complexes on the empty small site are zero (the empty covering forces the group of sections on its sole object to be zero), so this bound holds as well. In particular it holds for every $U_i$ and $T_i$. Pullbacks of $G$ are torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion]; there is no finite coefficient ring, constructibility, invertibility, or fixed exponent assumption in the dimension theorem.

For part 1, the $U_i$ are qcqs by step 4, and the transition maps are affine as stipulated in the presentation. Step 6 bounds their torsion cohomological dimensions by the same $e_X$. Applying [lem-sc-cd-affine-limit] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{m tor}(U)\le e_X$. Let $u:U	o X$ and put $G_U=u_{\Et}^{-1}G$, which is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion]. The comparison-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $u_{\Proet}^{-1}
u_X^*G$ with $
u_U^*G_U$. For compatibility with the source restriction notation, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the slice over $U$ with $U_{\Proet}$. The inverse image formula in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] equals restriction here: for an object $W	o U$, the index category of maps $W	o Z	imes_XU$ has initial object $Z=W$ with its graph map; the opposite indexing category therefore has terminal object $W$. The presheaf colimit is $F(W)$ with its restriction maps and is already a sheaf by the localization equivalence. Apply the global-sections comparison of [sk-prop-sf-comparison] with the discrete ring $\mathbf Z$ and the complex $G_U[0]$: it gives $H^q(U_{\Proet},
u_U^*G_U)=H^q(U_{\Et},G_U)=0$ for $q>e_X$. This proves part 1 without claiming that $U$ is of finite type.

source.place: Part (1): affine limit and cohomology comparison

proof.text: For part 2, put $T=X\times_YV$ and $T_i=X\times_YV_i$. The canonical equality $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ follows directly from the universal properties: a map to either side is a map to $X$ and a compatible family of maps to $V_i$ whose composites to $Y$ agree. The transition $T_j\to T_i$ is the base change of the affine map $V_j\to V_i$, by the same fibre-product universal property. It is affine by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], applied with $V_j\to V_i$ and $T_i\to V_i$. Each $T_i$ is qcqs by step 4 and has torsion dimension at most $e_X$ by step 6. Thus [lem-sc-cd-affine-limit] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(T)\le e_X$. This use of the limit lemma imposes no finite-type assumption on $V$ or $T$.

source.place: Part (2): base change of the affine limit; Stacks Tag 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine)

proof.text:
Let $t:T	o X$. Set $G_T=t_{\Et}^{-1}G$. It is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion], and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $(
u_X^*G)|_T$ with $
u_T^*G_T$. Apply [sk-prop-sf-comparison] on the scheme $T$, with coefficients $\mathbf Z$ and $G_T[0]$. Together with step 8 this gives $H^q(T_{\Proet},(
u_X^*G)|_T)=H^q(T_{\Et},G_T)=0$ for $q>e_X$, proving part 2. The comparison is valid on an arbitrary scheme, and is only being used on a sheaf placed in degree zero, not on an unbounded complex.

source.place: Part (2): comparison for the actual pulled-back coefficient

proof.text: For part 3, [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] identifies $R^qg_{\Et,*}G$ with the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^q(X\times_YW,G)$, where this initially means derived section-evaluation on the object $X\times_YW$ of $X_{\Et}$. The object is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] and the slice-site equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]; together with [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], they identify this group with $H^q((X\times_YW)_{\Et},a_{\Et}^{-1}G)$ for its projection $a$ to $X$. For affine étale $W\to Y$, the finite-type and dimension arguments of steps 4–6 give zero for $q>e_X$. Every étale object of $Y$ has an affine open covering, itself an étale covering; hence every section of the displayed presheaf restricts to zero on a covering. The presheaf therefore sheafifies to zero, as required: any map from it to an abelian sheaf sends each section to a locally zero section, which is zero by the separatedness axiom; the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] then forces the identity of its sheafification to be zero. The sheafification theorem has no qcqs hypothesis on $g$.

source.place: Part (3): higher-direct-image presheaf and affine étale basis

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, then $U$, every $T_i$, and $X\times_YV$ are empty. The only abelian sheaf on their small sites is zero by the empty covering axiom, so all cohomology groups in parts 1–2 vanish. The direct-image functor from the zero abelian category is zero, and its right derived functors are zero, proving part 3. Thus $e_X=1$ is a valid bound in this case and excludes no scheme. Finally the preceding argument was for an arbitrary finite-type source and target over $k$. Repeat it with source $Y$, any torsion sheaf on $Y$, and an arbitrary finite-type map from $Y$ to a finite-type $k$-scheme. This gives the promised $e_Y$ assertions. Taking the identity map suffices for the absolute assertion for $Y$.
